prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

Disclosed is a method for processing cocoa beans or nibs comprising the steps of: (a) adding water to cocoa beans or nibs to form a suspension; (b) wet grinding said suspension; (c) subjecting said suspension to a heat treatment at a temperature of 70° C. or less; (d) separating the suspension into: a water phase (heavy phase), a fat phase (light phase) comprising cocoa butter, and a solid phase comprising cocoa powder and fluid components; (e) continuously separating the fluid components from the solid phase obtained in step (d) to obtain cocoa aroma and cocoa powder by supplying a flow of said solid phase to a mixing device; wherein the mixing device comprises: a cylindrical, tubular body with a horizontal axis having an inlet opening for the solid phase, an outlet opening for the dried solid phase and an optional outlet opening for a vapor phase comprising cocoa aroma; end plates closing the tubular body at its opposite ends; a coaxial jacket heating or cooling the internal wall of the tubular body to a temperature of from 55° C. to 150° C.; and a bladed rotor, which is supported for rotation in the tubular body, its blades being arranged as a helix and oriented for centrifuging the solid phase and simultaneously transporting it towards the outlet opening.

The method relates to the processing of cocoa beans or cocoa nibs in order to obtain valuable cocoa fractions, including cocoa butter, cocoa powder, and cocoa aroma. In this process, the cocoa beans or nibs are first combined with water to form an aqueous suspension. This suspension is then subjected to wet grinding, which reduces the particle size of the cocoa material and promotes the release of cocoa components into the surrounding liquid phase. After grinding, the suspension is exposed to a heat treatment carried out at a temperature of 70° C. or less. This controlled thermal treatment helps preserve desirable flavor and aroma compounds while preparing the material for subsequent separation steps.

Following the grinding and heat treatment, the treated suspension is separated into three main fractions. These include a heavy water phase, a light fat phase, and a solid phase. The heavy water phase primarily contains water-soluble components extracted from the cocoa material. The light fat phase contains cocoa butter, which separates due to its lower density. The solid phase contains cocoa powder together with remaining fluid components, including moisture and volatile or semi-volatile aroma constituents.

The solid phase is then further processed to continuously separate the remaining fluid components from the cocoa solids. This separation makes it possible to recover cocoa aroma while also producing cocoa powder with the desired physical and compositional characteristics. The continuous removal of fluid components improves process efficiency and allows the cocoa powder and aroma fractions to be obtained in a controlled and consistent manner.

To carry out this step, the solid phase is introduced into a specially designed mixing device. The device comprises a substantially horizontal cylindrical tubular body provided with an inlet opening for receiving the solid phase and an outlet opening for discharging the processed cocoa powder. The tubular body is closed at its ends by end plates. In some embodiments, the device may also include a vapor outlet, through which volatile cocoa aroma components can be removed and recovered during processing.

The mixing device may be equipped with a jacket through which a heating or cooling medium is circulated. This allows the temperature of the cocoa material inside the device to be regulated according to the requirements of the process. Within the tubular body, a rotor fitted with helical blades is arranged along the longitudinal axis. As the rotor turns, the helical blades mix and transport the solid phase from the inlet toward the outlet. At the same time, the rotation generates a centrifuging action, distributing the material against the inner wall of the tubular body and promoting the separation of fluid components from the cocoa solids.

By combining mechanical transport, mixing, centrifugal action, and controlled heating or cooling, the device enables efficient treatment of the solid cocoa phase. The result is the recovery of cocoa aroma from the separated fluid components and the production of cocoa powder from the remaining solids, while cocoa butter and the aqueous phase are obtained from the earlier separation of the treated suspension.
outputs.L4:
The method relates to the processing of cocoa beans, cocoa nibs, or comparable cocoa raw materials in a way that allows the principal cocoa constituents to be separated efficiently while preserving valuable flavor and aroma components. In the process, water is first added to the cocoa material to form an aqueous suspension. The cocoa beans or nibs may be pretreated, broken, shelled, or otherwise prepared before the addition of water. The resulting mixture is then subjected to wet grinding, producing a finely divided cocoa suspension in which the cocoa solids, cocoa fat, water-soluble components, and aroma substances are dispersed.

After wet grinding, the suspension is exposed to a mild heat treatment. This heat treatment is controlled so that the cocoa material is warmed sufficiently to support separation and microbiological stabilization, but not so severely that desirable cocoa aromas are lost or degraded. The temperature and residence time may be selected according to the type of cocoa material being processed and the desired flavor profile of the final products.

The treated suspension is then separated into three main phases: an aqueous phase, a fat phase, and a solid phase. The fat phase contains cocoa butter, which can be recovered and further purified or processed. The aqueous phase contains water-soluble cocoa components and may also contain volatile aroma compounds. These aroma compounds can be recovered, concentrated, and optionally reintroduced into cocoa products or used separately as natural cocoa flavoring. The solid phase contains the defatted or partially defatted cocoa solids that are suitable for producing cocoa powder.

A particular feature of the method is the further continuous treatment of the separated solid phase in a bladed-rotor mixing device. This device may be heated or cooled depending on the desired processing conditions. The rotating blades continuously mix, convey, knead, and condition the cocoa solids, allowing moisture to be removed in a controlled manner and preventing the formation of large agglomerates. By adjusting parameters such as rotor speed, temperature, residence time, and pressure, the solid phase can be dried and converted into a stable cocoa powder with the desired particle structure and moisture content.

Because the process separates cocoa into water, fat, and solid fractions at an early stage, it permits efficient recovery of cocoa butter and facilitates the drying of the cocoa solids. At the same time, the use of wet processing and mild heat treatment helps preserve sensitive flavor constituents. Volatile cocoa aroma released during processing can be captured rather than lost, improving the overall value and quality of the resulting products.

The process therefore provides a practical and efficient way to obtain cocoa butter, cocoa powder, and recoverable cocoa aroma from cocoa beans or nibs. It combines effective phase separation with controlled continuous drying or conditioning of the cocoa solids, resulting in high-quality cocoa products while reducing losses of desirable flavor components.

**Disclosed**

The word **“disclosed”** refers to something that has been revealed, made known, or shared openly. It is often used when information that was previously private, hidden, or confidential becomes available to others.

In business, legal, and financial contexts, disclosed information can include important facts, risks, agreements, or personal details that must be communicated clearly. For example, a company may disclose its financial results to investors, or a person may be required to disclose certain information before signing a contract.

Disclosure is important because it promotes transparency, trust, and accountability. When information is properly disclosed, people can make informed decisions based on accurate and complete details. However, some disclosed information may be sensitive, so it must be handled carefully and responsibly.

In everyday life, “disclosed” can also refer to personal honesty. When someone discloses their feelings, experiences, or concerns, they are choosing to be open and truthful. Whether in professional settings or personal relationships, disclosure plays a key role in communication and understanding.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a concise “Disclosed is…” description of an invention for separating cocoa butter, cocoa powder, and cocoa aroma from cocoa beans, including details of the cylindrical tubular mixing device used to remove fluid components from the solid phase.
counterfactuals.output: Disclosed is a process and apparatus for separating cocoa beans into cocoa butter, cocoa powder, and cocoa aroma. The process includes comminuting or grinding cocoa beans or nibs to form a cocoa mass, heating and/or conditioning the cocoa mass to liberate fat and volatile aroma components, and introducing the mass into a cylindrical tubular mixing device in which fluid components are separated from the solid cocoa phase. The tubular mixing device comprises an elongated cylindrical housing having an inlet for the cocoa mass, at least one outlet for a liquid cocoa butter-containing phase, at least one outlet for a volatile cocoa aroma-containing phase, and a discharge for a defatted solid cocoa phase. A rotatable shaft disposed along the longitudinal axis of the housing carries mixing, conveying, scraping, or kneading elements configured to continuously agitate the cocoa mass, renew exposed surfaces, and promote removal of liquid and gaseous components from the solids. The housing may be heated and may be operated under reduced pressure, inert gas flow, or controlled temperature conditions to enhance separation of cocoa butter and recovery of cocoa aroma while limiting thermal degradation. The resulting solid phase is processed to cocoa powder, the liquid phase is recovered as cocoa butter, and the volatile phase is condensed or absorbed to obtain cocoa aroma.

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a patent abstract/claim for cocoa bean processing where water is added to form a suspension, the suspension is wet-ground and heated at no more than 70°C, separated into heavy, light, and solid phases, and the solid phase is continuously processed in a heated horizontal rotor dryer.
counterfactuals.output:
## Abstract

A process for processing cocoa beans or cocoa nibs is provided, comprising adding water to comminuted cocoa bean material to form an aqueous suspension, wet-grinding the suspension while maintaining the suspension at a temperature of not more than 70°C, and separating the ground suspension into a heavy phase, a light phase, and a solid phase. The solid phase is subsequently processed continuously in a heated horizontal rotor dryer to reduce moisture content and obtain a dried cocoa solid product. The process enables controlled low-temperature treatment of cocoa material, efficient phase separation, and continuous drying of the solid fraction while preserving desirable cocoa components.

## Claim

1. A method of processing cocoa bean material, comprising:  
   adding water to cocoa bean material to form an aqueous suspension;  
   wet-grinding the aqueous suspension while heating or maintaining the aqueous suspension at a temperature of not more than 70°C;  
   separating the wet-ground suspension into at least three phases comprising a heavy phase, a light phase, and a solid phase; and  
   continuously feeding the solid phase to a heated horizontal rotor dryer and drying the solid phase therein to produce a dried cocoa solid product.
